STORAGE & HANDLING GUIDE
BITUMEN STORAGE & HANDLING FOR IMPORT BUYERS

LAST REVIEWED SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 · PETROBIND EXPORT DESK

Correct storage protects the value of a qualified shipment. Bitumen that is overheated, under-heated, or exposed to moisture during storage can lose the properties confirmed on its COA before it ever reaches a paving or roofing project.

Request Bitumen Quote
View Bitumen Grades
DRUM STORAGE BASICS

Drummed bitumen should be stored under cover, away from direct sun and open flame, ideally on a level, load-bearing surface. Steel drums store well at ambient temperature; softening or leakage usually signals excessive heat exposure or a compromised seal, not a product fault.

BULK AND MOLTEN STORAGE

Bulk or bitutainer buyers need insulated, temperature-controlled tanks with agitation or circulation to prevent hard-skinning and localized overheating. Molten storage temperature should track the grade-specific softening point guidance on the PDS — exceeding it risks oxidation and property drift; running too cold risks unpumpable, hardened material.

Keep molten storage within the grade's recommended temperature band, not a single generic figure.

Avoid repeated heating/cooling cycles — they accelerate hardening.

Inspect tank insulation and circulation before a bulk delivery, not after.

HANDLING AND SAFETY

Hot bitumen causes serious thermal burns; handling teams should use heat-resistant PPE, and any molten transfer should follow a documented safe work procedure. Cooled, solid bitumen presents low acute hazard, but fumes from overheated material can still irritate — ventilation matters during heating and loading.
